The main takeaway from our work is that

, for objects with negative-curvature regions, the grasp quality is not only determined by the contact points, but also by the shape of the grasping surface, and that a planner exploiting this information can find grasps more effective than those based on the contact points alone.
, when grasping objects with negative curvature, it is important to consider the shape of the object in the planning process.
, when dealing with concave objects, grasping planners should explicitly consider the negative curvature of the objects, and use it to guide the search for grasps.
